title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Base Premium and the Insured Value It Starts From
content:
The premium of a cover under `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims` is anchored to an Insured Value, and which Insured Value depends on when the premium falls due.

## Definition

The **base premium** is an Insured Value multiplied by the tier's premium rate percentage. The base premium is not rounded.

## Which Insured Value

- **Premium falling due after binding.** The starting point is the Insured Value fixed when the cover was bound, and that value alone. A figure appearing on a quote is an estimate and is never the starting point of such a premium; an unbound cover offers no bound value from which a base premium of this kind could be taken.
- **Premium owed ahead of binding.** Where a cash-in-advance holder must pay ahead of binding because the tier requires prepayment, the premium is built in the same way on the Insured Value that the cover carries on the line's records.

## Worked examples (hypothetical rates and values)

| Insured Value used (USD) | Premium rate (percent) | Base premium (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| 150000.00 | 0.20 | 300.00 |
| 66666.67 | 0.30 | 200.00001 |
| 250000.00 | 0.05 | 125.00 |

The second row is carried forward as 200.00001, since the base premium is not rounded.
